corrected_value.title: Believe Me, I Have No Idea What I’m Talking About: The Effects of Source Certainty on Consumer Involvement and Persuasion
corrected_value.title_o: Believe Me, I Have No Idea What I’m Talking About: The Effects of Source Certainty on Consumer Involvement and Persuasion

decisions.quote:
In this Registered Report, we conducted a highpowered (N = 1018) direct replication of Experiment 2 by Karmarkar and Tormala (2010). In a consumer
behaviour context, the original study examined whether source expertise moderated the positive effect of source
certainty on the persuasive impact of a restaurant recommendation.
decisions.location: Abstract, p. 1, lines 33-35 (see also Section 2, p. 2, lines 176-206; Section 4.2, p. 4, lines 495-504; References, p. 12, lines 1549-1551)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding accurately identify Karmarkar and Tormala (2010), Journal of Consumer Research, DOI 10.1086/648381, as the replicated original study (primarily targeting Experiment 2, along with the expectancy-violation measure from Experiment 1).

decisions.quote:
Overall, we must
conclude that our study failed to replicate the findings in the original,
and that we find support for the confidence heuristic hypothesis (H1b)
rather than the incongruity hypothesis (H1a).
decisions.location: Section 8 (Discussion), p. 11, lines 1440-1443 (see also Abstract, p. 1, lines 35-39; Section 7.1, pp. 7-9, lines 976-1172)
decisions.reason: Per Step 3 Rule 1 of the codebook, the authors' explicit overall verdict governs. The authors state that their study failed to replicate the original findings, finding no expertise x certainty interaction on attitudes (F(1, 506) = 0.84, p = .361), an opposite-direction effect for experts (d = 0.28, p = .027), and no support for the proposed expectancy-violation mechanism.

decisions.quote: In this Registered Report, we conducted a highpowered (N = 1018) direct replication of Experiment 2 by Karmarkar and Tormala (2010).
decisions.location: Abstract, p. 1, line 33 (see also Section 6.2, p. 4, lines 518-520)
decisions.reason: The study collected new empirical data from 1018 US participants on Prolific to re-test the published findings of Karmarkar and Tormala (2010), which meets the codebook definition of a replication.
